samples.summary: The docKey→documentId rule is re-implemented in four places, and two same-named `documentIdOf` functions now give different answers to the same question
samples.evidence:
`wafflebase-doc-store.ts:229` already *exports* `documentKeyOf()` — and its own comment says why: "Defined here because this module is where store keys are consumed, and two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false." The change then adds three more copies rather than importing it:

- `offline-copy.ts:52` `documentIdOf()` — splits on `/`, returns the last segment (`"note-7"`). This is `documentKeyOf` reimplemented verbatim under a different name.
- `offline-erase.ts:390-394` `documentIdOf()` — same name, but additionally strips the type prefix, returning `"7"`.
- `wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1012-1013` — the same `indexOf("-")` / `slice(dash + 1)` prefix strip, inlined in `storedDocumentIds`.
- `offline-copy-recovery.ts` `describeArchivedDocument()` — a fourth variant, with its own `TYPE_PREFIXES` table, that answers `undefined` for prefixes the other three happily mangle (`pdf-`, `mystery`).

The two `documentIdOf`s disagree on their return value while sharing a name, and the store's prefix strip is the matching half of `purgeOfflineDocuments` → `purgeDocument` → `isDocument`: these must agree or a purge silently matches nothing. The file's own comment records that exact failure having already happened once on the lock-name/store-key pair. Consolidating on the exported `documentKeyOf` plus one exported `documentIdOf` beside it is the reuse this repo expects.

Related, and evidence of the confusion: `RecoverableWork.documentId` (`offline-copy.ts`) is populated from the last-segment variant, so it holds `"note-7"` rather than a document id, and is read by nothing in production — `offline-runtime.tsx` goes to `describeArchivedDocument(item.docKey)` instead. Only `offline-copy.test.ts:156` reads it.

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` (and self-`removeMember`) issue an extra `GET /workspaces/:ref` and an unfiltered `GET /documents` for every user, ungated by `supportsClientKey()` or the opt-in — breaking the "PR 4 is a dark launch" / "declining the opt-in costs nothing" property on a build where the feature cannot be enabled
samples.evidence:
`documentIdsIn(ref)` (workspaces.ts:101) runs `fetchWorkspace(ref)` then `fetchDocuments()` — an unfiltered listing of every document the caller can read — and `deleteWorkspace` awaits it unconditionally before the DELETE (line 127). `removeMember` does the same whenever the removed member is the signed-in user (line 160), which is the ordinary "leave workspace" case.

Neither is behind `supportsClientKey()` nor behind `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`, unlike every other consumer this change adds. `PrivateRoute.tsx:28` gates `OfflineRuntime` precisely on that reasoning, and `app/settings/page.tsx` and the chip's offer are gated too; the design doc states the rule as "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing" and "the promise that declining the opt-in costs nothing has to be kept by the housekeeping as much as by the client" (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Turning it on, § Storage).

On the currently pinned `@yorkie-js/react@0.7.22` the feature is entirely inert by design (§ Status: "no durable client mounts, no store is ever attached"), yet every workspace deletion and every self-removal on that build now costs two extra round trips, one of which lists the user's whole document set, purely to compute ids for a purge that `purgeOfflineDocuments` will immediately discard (`offlineUserId()` is undefined because `rememberOfflineUser` is only ever called by the unmounted `OfflineRuntime`). Gate `documentIdsIn` on the same predicate the rest of the feature uses.

samples.summary: Once the dependency is bumped, `OfflineRuntime` mounts for every signed-in user regardless of the opt-in, so declining will not "cost nothing"
samples.evidence:
`offlineInPlay = supportsClientKey() || getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(me?.id)`. `supportsClientKey()` is a build-time constant, so after the `@yorkie-js/react >= 0.7.23` bump that the design's § Status names as "the whole remaining action" this is unconditionally true and the left operand makes the preference check irrelevant.

`OfflineRuntime`'s effect then runs for every session of every signed-in user: it opens the IndexedDB database (`new WafflebaseDocStore(...)` → `open()` creates it), records the identity, runs `collectStale()`, and issues its own unfiltered `GET /documents` for the reconcile — for accounts that declined the feature and have nothing stored to sweep or reconcile.

The design doc contains both halves of this contradiction: § Storage says the runtime mounts "only where the feature is in play (`supportsClientKey()`, …)" while asserting in the same paragraph that "the promise that declining the opt-in costs nothing has to be kept by the housekeeping as much as by the client". The gate as written keeps the promise only while the feature is dark. A `supportsClientKey() && (enabled || anyConsentOnThisDevice)` shape would keep both.

samples.summary: The design doc claims the recovery path reuses `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`; the implementation reuses the *import* engine instead, and the See Also link asserts the wrong dependency
samples.evidence:
Line 646: "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and line 751: "[document-copy.md](document-copy.md) — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses".

`lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts` touches neither. It calls `createWorkspaceDocument()` and then `applyImportedContent()` (`app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts`), with a bespoke `writeNote()` for the note type. Nothing in the diff references `copyDocument` or the copy route.

The implementation choice looks right — `POST /documents/:id/copy` duplicates a *server-side* document by id, and an archive has no server-side source to copy from (one of the three archive causes is precisely that the source was deleted upstream) — so the doc is what is wrong, not the code. But the doc is the artefact a future reader reaches for, and it currently points them at the wrong module and the wrong sibling design doc. The real reuse is `apply-imported-content.ts` plus the per-type `Yorkie*Store` readers, and the See Also should say so.

samples.summary: `sync-status.md` § API shape was not updated for the hook's new nullable `state`, though this change makes it nullable and makes the chip render nothing
samples.evidence:
The doc's canonical signature still reads `state: SyncState;` (line 448) and `export function SyncStatusChip(props): JSX.Element;` (line 457). This change makes `useSyncStatus()` return `state: SyncState | null` (`use-sync-status.ts`, the new `if (error)` arm) and makes `SyncStatusChip` `return null` when `state === null`.

The diff does revise the states table and the `SyncState` union a few lines above, so the omission is an oversight in the same edit rather than a deliberate deferral. The behaviour is reasoned about in the *other* doc (offline-local-persistence.md § Non-Goals, "the sync chip says nothing on that screen"), but the hook's contract lives here, and the repo files docs by subsystem rather than by change. Every consumer now has to decide what to do with `null`; the documented shape says they do not.

Searched: `docs/design/sync-status.md` in full for `SyncState`, `state:`, `null`, `JSX.Element`; grepped `docs/design/` for `saved-locally` and `useSyncStatus`.

samples.summary: The README index row for `sync-status.md` still asserts offline persistence is deferred and that "the wording never claims local durability", which this change reverses
samples.evidence:
The diff inserts the new `offline-local-persistence.md` row (line 175) but leaves the `sync-status.md` row above it ending: "Offline persistence deferred — `@yorkie-js/sdk@0.7.20` added an opt-in `ClientOptions.store` but we pass none, and turning it on needs a stable `clientKey`, which activates the SDK's single-active-session guard and costs the second tab on an open document — which is why the wording never claims local durability".

All three clauses are now false as stated: `sync-status.md` itself has been edited in this same diff to strike the Non-Goal ("~~**Offline persistence.**~~ **No longer a Non-Goal**"), the second-tab cost is resolved by the app-owned election, and the chip now does claim local durability in the `saved-locally` row. The index is the entry point readers scan before opening anything, so the two adjacent rows now contradict each other.

Searched: `docs/design/README.md` for `sync-status`, `offline`, `durab`; diffed the README hunk — only an insertion, no edit to the preceding row.

samples.summary: The Settings navigation restructure (sidebar entry removed, new `SettingsDialog` mounted in `NavUser`) is scope beyond what any design doc describes
samples.evidence:
`offline-local-persistence.md` § Turning it on specifies two entry points and describes the first as "**Settings** — a switch, next to Appearance and Dates" — i.e. the existing Settings page. It says nothing about splitting `Settings` into `SettingsContent` + a new `components/settings-dialog.tsx`, adding a `Settings` item to the user dropdown, or deleting `/settings` from the sidebar's workspace-less branch (`use-workspace-nav-items.ts:53-57`).

That is a product-visible navigation change affecting every user on a build where the offline feature cannot even be enabled: the workspace-less shell loses its Settings entry, and the device settings become reachable only from the avatar menu. The justification is argued entirely in code comments (`use-workspace-nav-items.ts:31-38`, `settings-dialog.tsx`) rather than in a doc, and `docs/design/frontend.md:50` still documents `/settings → Settings` hanging off Layout with no mention of the dialog surface.

The reasoning is sound and the route is preserved, so the cost is contained — but per CONTRIBUTING this belongs folded into the canonical frontend/offline doc, not left as a comment-only decision discovered by whoever next edits the sidebar.

samples.summary: An unrelated spell-check fix in `@wafflebase/docs` is bundled into the offline-persistence change
samples.evidence:
`runSpellRecheck` is split into a swallowing wrapper plus `recheckSpelling`, with a session-identity guard added after the await. The stated motivation is a test-harness symptom: "under Vitest that import rejects with an `EnvironmentTeardownError` once the test environment is gone, which surfaced as an unhandled rejection that failed the whole frontend run while every test passed."

Nothing in this hunk touches offline persistence, the sync chip, or any module the rest of the diff adds, and no design doc in the change references the docs spell-check path. It is a legitimate fix, but carried in a branch this large it is invisible to anyone reviewing or bisecting the offline feature, and a revert of the feature would take it with it. It belongs in its own change.

samples.summary: `keepArchives` is a vestigial option with no caller, left over from the rejected "401 erases live entries" branch
samples.evidence:
`eraseOfflineData(store, userId, options: { keepArchives?: boolean })` (offline-erase.ts:30) forwards it to `WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1135, 1173), whose comment names its intended caller: "`keepArchives` is for the one caller that did not ask for any of this: a session the server expired."

That caller no longer exists. The design was revised so the 401 arm erases nothing at all (`eraseLocalData: "none"` in `api/auth.ts`, and the doc's cleanup table row "Session expired (401) | Nothing"), so grepping the whole of `packages/` finds only the two declarations and the comment — no call site ever passes it. knip does not flag unused properties of an options object, so nothing else will surface it. Either drop it or note in the doc that it is kept for a caller yet to exist.

samples.summary: A vitest suite lives in `src/lib/` under a non-test filename
samples.evidence:
`doc-store-contract.ts` imports `describe`/`it`/`expect` from vitest and exports `testDocStoreContract()`, a full suite body. It sits in the production source directory beside `wafflebase-doc-store.ts` rather than under a test path, so it dodges the `src/**/*.test.ts` include glob and only runs because `wafflebase-doc-store.test.ts` imports it.

The transcription itself is well justified in the file header (the SDK publishes only `dist`, so the upstream suite cannot be imported, and running the copy against `MemoryDocStore` is what detects drift). It is the placement that is odd — a shared test fixture under `lib/` invites a production module to import it, which would pull vitest into the app graph. A `src/lib/__tests__/` or `.fixture.ts` location would express the intent.

samples.summary: Wholesale quote-style reflow of several untouched files inflates the diff
samples.evidence:
`vite.config.ts`, `lib/utils.ts`, `components/__tests__/collab-document-provider.test.tsx` and parts of `collab-document-provider.tsx` are re-quoted double→single across their whole bodies, producing dozens of hunks with no semantic content — in `utils.ts` the entire diff is two trailing semicolons and two quote pairs. The surrounding repo (`PrivateRoute.tsx`, `nav-user.tsx`, `api/documents.ts`, the rest of `src/lib/`) is double-quoted, so this also leaves the new offline modules split between both conventions.

Formatting is write-only here and no lane checks it, so nothing will catch or correct this; the cost is purely that it buries the substantive hunks in an already very large change.

verdict.reason: All four re-implementations exist as described. `wafflebase-doc-store.ts:229` exports `documentKeyOf()` with a comment explicitly warning that "two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false". Despite that, `offline-copy.ts:52-55` re-declares the identical split-on-"/"-last-segment rule privately as `documentIdOf` (the file already imports from `./wafflebase-doc-store` at line 2, so reuse was available); `offline-erase.ts:390-395` declares a second function of the SAME NAME that additionally strips the type prefix, so the two `documentIdOf`s return different values for the same input ("note-7" vs "7"); `wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1011-1014` inlines that same prefix strip in `storedDocumentIds`, which is the matching half of the purge path (`offline-erase.ts:524-534` -> `purgeDocument` -> `isDocument` at `:978-982`) and must stay in lockstep or a purge silently matches nothing; and `offline-copy-recovery.ts:128-159` is a fourth variant with its own TYPE_PREFIXES table that answers `undefined` where the others mangle. The divergence is not hypothetical: `RecoverableWork.documentId` is documented at `offline-copy.ts:40-41` as "Just the document id" but holds "note-7", as the only reader `offline-copy.test.ts:156` asserts. Duplication/reuse is explicitly in the design-fit lane, and "duplicated logic that will now diverge and give two answers to the same question" is the rubric's named major criterion. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as quoted, is reachable from production (offline-runtime.tsx:215/252/267), and nothing guards it.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described. `documentIdsIn` (workspaces.ts:101-115) issues `GET /workspaces/:ref` plus the unfiltered `GET /documents` (documents.ts:35-41), and `deleteWorkspace` awaits it unconditionally at workspaces.ts:127 with no `supportsClientKey()` or `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` guard anywhere in the file. That directly diverges from the rule the design doc states for the identical listing — offline-local-persistence.md:368-372 ("OfflineRuntime is mounted only where the feature is in play … the promise that declining the opt-in costs nothing has to be kept by the housekeeping as much as by the client"), :223-225, and :700-701 (PR 4 dark launch) — and from the shape the rest of the change follows (PrivateRoute.tsx:28-30,58 gates the same unfiltered GET /documents on exactly that predicate, with the reasoning spelled out at PrivateRoute.tsx:39-57). With the pin at @yorkie-js/react 0.7.22 (package.json:66) below MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23 (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24), the ids feed a purge that returns immediately (offline-erase.ts:412-415), so the round trips are pure cost. The reviewer's removeMember half is looser than the code — workspaces.ts:159-160 gates on `isOfflineUser`, which is false on an inert build since `rememberOfflineUser` is only called from offline-runtime.tsx:66 — but on a capable build PrivateRoute mounts OfflineRuntime for users who declined the opt-in as well, so that path also charges non-opted-in users, and `deleteWorkspace` is ungated for everyone in any case. No guard, absence, or scope argument refutes it.
